Hi Alex / Tanya —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a proposed path to nail down the performance & SLA items you flagged so the procurement and engineering teams can move forward.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Target workload: conversational triage + structured extraction for clinical intake (avg 60 tokens output, 150 input).
- Desired latency: P95 <= 350ms for single-request streaming-first-token, with 3 concurrent chat sessions per healthcare operator.
- Throughput: expected steady-state 120 qps during peak windows (regional), with burst to 300 qps for brief periods.
- Durability: strict audit logs and exportable metrics for every request for compliance.

Questions we need to finalize for SLO/SLA wording:
1) Do you want latency measured as time-to-first-token (streaming) or time-to-last-token (end-to-end)?
2) Are warm-up / cold-starts acceptable to exclude for the first N minutes after deployment, and if so what N?
3) What SL reporting cadence do procurement/ops expect (weekly CSV, daily API, or monthly summary)?

Next steps (proposed):
- Priyom & Vivek will draft a performance profile mapping your workload to model variants and expected P95/P99 under continuous batching.
- We’ll prepare an SLA draft that clarifies measurement definitions, standard exclusions (scheduled maintenance, force majeure, customer network issues), and remedy calculations for credits.
- Procurement: if acceptable, Alex/Tanya to share the contact for the procurement queue (cc procurement@acmepharma.com).

I attached the Acme MVP requirements you shared and an initial Redwood SLA template (v1) — Priyom/Vivek, please flag anything we should change before sharing with Acme.

Thanks,

Soojin Lee

Thanks Soojin — really helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: prefer P95 time-to-first-token for streaming scenarios (we care most about operator experience). For non-streaming batch jobs, we can use end-to-end.
- Cold starts: we'd like the SLA to exclude cold-starts for the first 5 minutes after a deployment or scaling event. Can you confirm Redwood's typical cold-start behaviour for the dedicated pool?
- Reporting: procurement wants weekly CSV exports, but ops will want an API we can poll daily. Can those both be supported?

One more ask: in the remedy section, we need clear examples — e.g., how credits are calculated for sustained P95 breaches vs single-window spikes. Procurement will push back on vague language.

I'll loop procurement in once we have the SLA language and perf profile.

Alex — quick answers from the infra side and some numbers to set expectations.

1) Measurement definitions: we can report both metrics. For streaming-first-token P95 we measure from the time the request hits our gateway to the time the first token is emitted from the model-serving runtime. For end-to-end we measure until final token commit. Both are available via our telemetry pipeline.

2) Cold starts & exclusions: for Dedicated pools we maintain warmed workers; cold-starts are rare but can happen during autoscale events. We propose excluding a 5-minute window after any scaling event or deploy (matches your ask). We can also surface warm pool size and scaling logs in the report.

3) Throughput & concurrency: given your target (120 steady qps, 300 burst), recommended configuration is a dedicated pool with 8x A100-class GPUs, autoscale to +50% for bursts. Expected P95 estimates (model dependent) under continuous batching:
   - Model A (quantized): P95 first-token ~ 220–360ms at 1–3 concurrency per session at 150 token effective sequence length
   - Model B (higher quality): P95 first-token ~ 300–520ms under same load
Actual numbers vary by prompt distribution; we'll run a small benchmark with a representative prompt set you provided (thanks for the sample file).

4) Reporting cadence: we can export weekly CSVs for procurement and provide a daily metrics API for ops. We also support webhooks for alerting if any SLO breaches occur.

5) Remedies: standard remedy model is service-credit based and tiered by severity and duration. Example language we propose for the draft SLA: credit = (monthly invoice) * breach_fraction, where breach_fraction is calculated from the percentage of measured samples exceeding P95 over the billing month, excluding maintenance windows and documented exclusions. We'll draft concrete examples for single-window spikes vs sustained breaches.

I'll prepare the perf profile and push an updated SLA draft to the Drive link. Vivek and Rishi will include guidance on streaming-first-token vs end-to-end monitoring hooks.

—Priyom
